fills.researcher_notes: COMPANY-level Operator question, established once for this brief's ETP-Legacy-owned Texas intrastate rows (P0180, P0203, and to a lesser extent P0250/P0258 which are separately-branded systems, see those shards) and applied here. Sheet Owner = 'ETP Legacy [100.%]' (GEM's owner-vocabulary name for Energy Transfer's legacy intrastate-Texas entity). Energy Transfer LP's FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026, CIK 1276187), Item 1 Business, describes its Intrastate Transportation and Storage segment as operating ~12,200 miles of intrastate gas pipe in Texas/Oklahoma/Louisiana, and specifically describes Texas intrastate assets including gathering and transport of 'East Texas' Haynesville-area production (Ark-La-Tex gathering assets 'in several parishes in northwest Louisiana and several counties in East Texas') and a '36-inch East Texas extension' of the Katy Pipeline connecting the Reed (Freestone Co.) and Grimes Co. compressor stations -- consistent with this row's route (Texas-to-Texas), 2008 StartYear1 (Haynesville-shale build-out era) and 2400 MMcf/d capacity range. The 10-K does not use 'East Texas Gas Pipeline' as a single distinct named asset (Energy Transfer's named Texas systems in this filing are the ET Fuel System, HPL System, Katy Pipeline and its East Texas extension, RIGS, Comanche Trail, Trans-Pecos, Red Bluff Express, Pelico and Lobo) -- so this row most likely corresponds to part of one of those named systems (most plausibly the ET Fuel System or the Katy Pipeline's East Texas extension) rather than being a wiki-only construct, but I could not pin the row to one specific named sub-system with confidence. I searched Texas Railroad Commission's public GIS pipeline viewer and T-4 permit index, naturalgasintel.com and OGJ for an independent (non-Energy-Transfer) operator confirmation of this specific line and found none that names 'East Texas Gas Pipeline' by that title -- RRC records intrastate lines under operator-filed system names that don't map 1:1 to GEM's route-level naming, and no dedicated third-party profile of this line exists. The only usable source is Energy Transfer's own 10-K (single origin, SEC filer CIK 1276187) -- staged at tier=medium/independent=false, honestly reflecting single-origin sourcing. A human should treat 'Energy Transfer' as well-supported at the company level (matches Owner = ETP Legacy 100%) but note that no independent, line-specific corroboration was found, and that the exact sub-system identity within Energy Transfer's Texas intrastate network remains open.
